card.name: Contemporary dance
card.tagline: Genre-blending concert dance born from modern dance and ballet
card.profile: Contemporary dance is a genre of concert dance that developed during the mid-twentieth century and has grown into one of the dominant genres for formally trained dancers worldwide, especially in the U.S. and Europe (Wikipedia). It evolved out of and in reaction to modern dance and ballet, drawing on the legacies of Martha Graham, Merce Cunningham - who presented his first solo New York concert in April 1944 with composer John Cage, his life partner and frequent collaborator until Cage's death in 1992 - and German Tanztheater figures such as Pina Bausch (Wikipedia; Merce Cunningham Trust). It blends ballet legwork with modern dance's torso emphasis, plus contract-release, floorwork, improvisation and release technique, and freely absorbs non-Western forms such as African dance and Japanese Butoh (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Per the New Grove and the International Encyclopedia of Dance, contemporary dance is defined less by fixed steps than by innovation and the collapse of distinctions between composition and improvisation (Wikipedia).

steps.name: brush
steps.description: brush right arm up as if painting a wall

steps.name: plie frame
steps.description: bend knees and create a frame with hands

steps.name: thread
steps.description: right arm reaches through the middle and high

steps.name: sway
steps.description: sway to the right and left

steps.name: lift chin
steps.description: lift up and lift your chin

steps.name: pot de bourree
steps.description: step right foot, left foot crosses behind, step right foot

images: creating a frame with your hands
kiss together like a little mermaid
common_mistakes: not dropping the head when clasping hands
not lifting the chin with the hands
lessons.teacher_style: The teacher uses a friendly, encouraging tone to make contemporary dance accessible to beginners. She breaks down complex movements into smaller, manageable parts and provides clear, descriptive imagery to guide the student.
lessons.distinctive_method: The teacher uses a 'pot de bourree' as a transition step between sections.
what_works: The teacher breaks down the routine into small, manageable sections.
The teacher uses clear, descriptive imagery to explain the movements.
what_hinders: The teacher does not always mirror the movements, which can be confusing for beginners.

observation.setting: A large theatre stage with an audience and judges panel in front of a giant LED screen, during a talent show audition.
observation.formation_and_space: Soloist moving across the center stage, travelling diagonally and circularly
observation.posture: Erect upright torso transitioning into expressive fluid bends and contractions, weight shifts between legs with soft knees and bare feet
observation.footwork: Ballet-inspired steps including relevés, extended leg extensions, glides, and floor transitions timed to the vocal beats
observation.arms_and_hands: Fluid, expressive arm movements extending outwards, framing the body, and graceful hand gestures
observation.hips_and_torso: Flexible spinal articulation, contractions, arches, and fluid torso twists
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Dynamic turns, leaps, high leg extensions, floor work including kneeling and splits
observation.costume_and_props: Sparkling light blue leotard with sheer sleeves and a short pleated skirt, hair tied in a bun with hair accessories
observation.cannot_infer: Exact acoustic properties of the venue and subtle breath control cannot be inferred from compressed video
